 US crude declines 4.43% to $91.85 a barrel, while European benchmark natural gas futures fall 4.59% amid diplomatic efforts to ease US-Iran tensions Mucahithan Avcioglu 04 November 2026 • Update : 04 November 2026 ISTANBUL Brent crude fell below $100 a barrel Wednesday for the first time in a month, extending losses for a third consecutive session amid diplomatic efforts to resolve the US-Iran conflict.
 The international benchmark declined $4.90, or 4.73%, to $98.70 a barrel as of 1615GMT.
 US benchmark West Texas Intermediate crude fell $4.26, or 4.43%, to $91.85 a barrel, its lowest level in about three weeks.
 European natural gas prices also declined, reversing earlier gains.
 Dutch Title Transfer Facility futures, Europe's benchmark for natural gas, dropped 4.59% to €87.40 ($98.10) per megawatt-hour after trading above €93 earlier Wednesday.
 The energy price declines followed Democrats' victory in Tuesday's US midterm elections, which gave the party control of Congress, as Qatar and Pakistan continued diplomatic efforts to ease tensions between Washington and Tehran.
 Qatari Foreign Ministry spokesperson Majed Al Ansari said Tuesday that both sides were reviewing proposals following approximately three hours of talks between a Qatari delegation and Iranian officials in Tehran on Monday.
 Al Ansari said the willingness of Washington and Tehran to continue discussions offered a "glimmer of hope," although mediators had yet to achieve a breakthrough.
 He also condemned the targeting of the Qatari gas carrier Al Mayeda, warning that attacks on vessels in the Gulf threatened regional security and complicated negotiations.
 Meanwhile, European natural gas storage facilities were less than 75% full, with forecasts of colder weather expected to increase heating demand across northwestern Europe.
 Germany's gas storage facilities were approximately 61% full, below the government's 70% target.
